summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with mast cell degranulation syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and chronic pain presented with shortness of breath, flushing, and pruritus after a recent pneumonia. She had received IV antihistamines and opioids in the ED but re-presented with persistent symptoms. Evaluation showed stable vital signs, no signs of anaphylaxis, and a chest X-ray indicating resolving pneumonia. Concerns about inappropriate use of IV narcotics and benzodiazepines were confirmed through multidisciplinary review. She was managed with oral medications and IV Phenergan overnight, discontinued all IV therapies by early morning, and was discharged home asymptomatic. Mild hypercalcemia was noted, requiring outpatient follow-up. A written pain management plan with her pain specialist was emphasized for future admissions. Follow-up was arranged for lung and splenic lesions.
